setup_summary.text: Fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter to 2026-07-31) revenue was $11.35B, up 10.8% year on year, and six-month revenue was $22.48B, up 12.0%. Informatica, acquired in November 2025, contributed about $456M in Q2, which is roughly 4 points of that growth. It stays in the Q3 comparison and only laps in Q4.

Q2 operating income was flat at about $2.33B, so operating margin fell to 20.5% from 22.8%. Restructuring rose to $94M from $4M and subscription cost of revenue rose to 18% of revenue from 16%, on hosting and generative AI spend. Intangible amortization was $522M, up from $380M.

Q2 diluted EPS of $4.29 (vs $1.96) is not a clean run-rate. It includes $2.61B of gains on strategic investments, of which $2.7B were unrealized gains on Anthropic. Management says strategic-investment gains and losses moved six-month diluted EPS by $2.87, and the ASR added $0.57.

The balance sheet was re-levered in March 2026. Debt principal rose to $39.5B from $14.5B. The company issued $25B of senior notes in March 2026 and used the proceeds to fund a $25B accelerated share repurchase (ASR). It also entered a $6B term loan in March 2026. Q2 interest expense was $473M vs $67M, and management expects interest expense above the prior-year level throughout FY27. Q2 diluted shares were 821M vs 962M.

Demand indicators at the Q2 balance sheet date: current RPO was $33.5B, up 14% year on year with minimal FX effect, and total RPO was $66.3B, up 11%. Attrition was about 8%, consistent with the prior year. Pricing was not a significant driver of subscription growth.

Per a 2026-10-30 news report, management guided fiscal Q3 2027 revenue to $11.42B-$11.5B, excluding the Contentful and Fin acquisitions. Consensus revenue is $11.57B, above the top of the range. Against the $10.26B year-ago quarter, the guide implies roughly +11.3% to +12.1% growth, and consensus implies +12.8%. The Street is therefore pricing a beat versus the guide.

The report is due 2026-12-01 after the close, per the market-data calendar, though the date is not confirmed. The average closing move over the last 8 reports was ±6.8%. No options-implied move or whisper EPS is available.

On 2026-10-20 Salesforce agreed to buy Braze for about $5.66B enterprise value ($47.50 per share in cash), closing in FY28. Salesforce said FY27 guidance is not expected to change and that it has not guided FY28. The slides flag growth accretion 'balanced by near term profitability dilution'.

since_filing.text: The only company filing after the 10-Q is the 2026-10-20 8-K (Items 7.01 and 9.01) on the Braze acquisition. It is not an earnings release and contains no quarterly results. The $5.66B enterprise value is $47.50 per share in cash, and Braze serves about 2,770 customers. No Braze revenue or profit figures are given.

Braze shares closed at $30.04 the day before the announcement, so the $47.50 offer is about a 58% premium (my arithmetic). Closing is expected in FY28, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

Cash commitments are growing. Contentful (about $1.5B) and Intercom/Fin (about $3.6B) were due to close in fiscal Q3, and Braze is about $5.66B of enterprise value. The three sum to about $10.8B (my arithmetic) against $11.4B of cash and marketable securities at 2026-07-31. Salesforce says the Braze deal will be cash-funded.
A 2026-10-30 article says Fin staff have since joined Salesforce, which suggests the Fin deal has closed. The Q3 revenue guide excludes Fin and Contentful, so they are potential upside to the guide.

ServiceNow reported Q3 2026 subscription revenue of $3.988B, up 21%, and raised its FY26 subscription revenue guidance to about $15.785B at the midpoint. Its stock reportedly fell about 26.7% on 2026-10-29 on an EPS miss ($1.00 vs $1.02) and Q4 cRPO growth guidance of 18.5%, below ~20% consensus. This is a single-source price move. It signals that growth deceleration is being punished in application software.

CRM has lagged the market. Shares were down 9.6% over 52 weeks against a 12% gain for the S&P 500, and market cap is about $190B. Of 52 analysts, 35 rate it Strong Buy, 13 Hold and 2 Strong Sell. The average price target is about $286.94, 25.3% above the price at the time of the article.
Full-year FY27 EPS consensus is $12.82 (+32.2%), then $11.53 for FY28 (-10.1%). The decline is consistent with FY27 including non-recurring investment gains, but the sources do not say so.

key_debates.question: Is organic growth reaccelerating, or is the headline helped by acquisitions?

bull.text: Current RPO was up 14% and Data 360, Headless Platform and Other grew 20%. Consensus Q3 growth of 12.8% would be a step up from Q2's 10.8%. Attrition is steady at about 8%.

bear.text: Agentforce Apps, 67% of subscription revenue, grew only 8%. Informatica added about $456M (about 4 points) in Q2. Professional services fell 4% and management says that may continue. The guide tops out below consensus.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 revenue versus the $11.5B top of the guide, how much of any beat comes from Fin and Contentful, Agentforce Apps growth, and cRPO growth ex-acquisitions.

key_debates.question: How good is the earnings quality after the Anthropic mark and the ASR?

bull.text: The ASR cut diluted shares to 821M from 962M and added $0.57 to six-month EPS. Consensus FY27 EPS of $12.82 is up 32%.

bear.text: Q2 operating income was flat and margin fell to 20.5% from 22.8%. Interest expense jumped to $473M from $67M. EPS leaned on $2.61B of strategic gains, mainly Anthropic, which is concentrated at about 45% of a portfolio that can reverse.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Q3 gap between GAAP operating income and net income, the strategic-investment line, the interest line, and whether the Street's EPS basis (unclear between $2.41 and $3.47) is met.

key_debates.question: Is the M&A pace and leverage manageable?

bull.text: The M&A framework requires a clear timeline for value accretion, and Salesforce says funding is in cash, which is non-dilutive. Free cash flow was $14.4B in FY26 and $7.65B in the first half of FY27.

bear.text: Debt is $39.5B with $6.0B due in FY29 and $4.25B in FY30. Pending cash deals include Contentful (~$1.5B), Fin (~$3.6B) and Braze (~$5.66B enterprise value), set against $11.4B of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. Management concedes near-term profitability dilution from Braze. Q2 interest expense was $473M.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 cash and debt balances, any new financing, quantified Braze dilution, and the pace of integration spend.

key_debates.question: Does ServiceNow's reaction signal a tougher bar for CRM?

bull.text: ServiceNow beat its own guide on subscription revenue, raised its FY subscription revenue outlook and lifted its AI ACV target. Its cRPO guide of 18.5% for Q4 came in below consensus and was cited in the selloff, alongside an EPS miss and AI fears. CRM's cRPO grew 14% with attrition steady at about eight percent.

bear.text: The market punished ServiceNow's cRPO guidance and EPS miss despite a revenue beat, and peers face seat-pricing and renewal-compression risk. HubSpot warns that consumption pricing is 'novel and evolving' with less predictability. CRM has lagged the S&P 500 and the Street sits above its guide.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 cRPO growth, Q4 and FY28 commentary on cRPO, and evidence of seat compression or consumption volatility in the call.

EPS is dominated by the strategic-investment line and the ASR share count, so the headline EPS comparison is noisy. Stock reaction is driven by cRPO and Q4 commentary.

Margin compresses further on AI and hosting costs and integration of three deals. Financing and leverage questions weigh on the shares.

claim.text: The bar is set above company guidance. Consensus revenue of $11.57B exceeds the $11.42B-$11.5B guide, so an in-line print against guidance may still read as a miss. Sentiment is fragile after ServiceNow's reaction.

Strategic investment concentration. Anthropic is about $5.1B, or roughly 45%, of the $11.3B portfolio (22% at year-end). Marks are non-linear, as a 10% fall in the five largest holdings would cut carrying value by about $641M. This line can swing GAAP EPS in either direction.

Leverage and financing. Debt principal is $39.5B vs $14.5B at year-end and interest expense is $473M a quarter. About $10.8B of announced acquisitions compare with $11.4B of cash and marketable securities, and may need more funding.

Margin pressure from AI. Total cost of revenues rose one percentage point as a share of revenue on hosting and generative AI spend plus intangible amortization, and management plans continued AI, agentic and cloud investment. The risk factors flag data center power, land and water constraints and possible suspension of access to frontier AI models.
Consumption pricing for Agentforce and Data 360 is harder to forecast, with attrition and revenue less predictable. HubSpot flags similar issues, and seat-based products face renewal compression.
ASR settlement exposure. Share price volatility may oblige Salesforce to deliver shares or make a cash payment on final settlement, expected in Q3.
Security risk from frontier AI models that can find zero-day vulnerabilities quickly, and the risk of emergency patching raising costs and disruption.

Backpage-related litigation keeps growing, with many new plaintiffs and actions. Most are stayed pending criminal proceedings. Management does not expect a material adverse impact but cannot estimate a range of loss. The Slack state action has reopened for discovery and class certification.

Integration and regulatory risk across pending acquisitions Contentful, Fin and Braze, with closings subject to regulatory approvals. Professional services revenue is declining (about -4%) on weaker demand for large transformation projects.

why.text: Subscription cost rose to 18% of revenue from 16% on hosting and generative AI spend, and management plans continued AI investment.

why.text: The 10-Q says complex pricing makes attrition and revenue harder to forecast, and peer risk factors point to seat-based renewal compression.

why.text: Anthropic is about 45% of the $11.3B portfolio and drove $2.7B of Q2 gains, which dominated reported EPS.
